# Modular Categories of Prime Power Dimension and Twisted Group Doubles

The central contribution of this work is the characterization of a natural class of modular categories whose Frobenius-Perron dimension is a prime power. Specifically, the authors identify these categories as the representation categories of twisted doubles of finite $p$-groups. This result situates a broad family of modular categories within a concrete, group-theoretical framework, providing an explicit structural description in terms of familiar algebraic objects.

A key structural tool underlying this characterization is the observation that nilpotent braided fusion categories admit an analogue of the classical Sylow decomposition. Just as a finite nilpotent group decomposes as the direct product of its Sylow $p$-subgroups, a nilpotent braided fusion category can be factored into components corresponding to distinct primes. This decomposition allows one to reduce the study of such categories to the prime power case, where the finer structural results apply.

Building on this foundation, the authors establish an important sufficient condition for a category to be group-theoretical. If the simple objects of the category have integral Frobenius-Perron dimensions, then the entire category is group-theoretical—that is, it can be realized in terms of the representation theory of finite groups equipped with suitable cohomological data. The integrality hypothesis thus serves as the crucial link between the abstract categorical structure and its concrete group-theoretical realization.

An important consequence of these results concerns semisimple quasi-Hopf algebras. As a corollary, the authors show that every semisimple quasi-Hopf algebra of prime power dimension is group-theoretical. This resolves the structural classification of such algebras in the prime power setting, demonstrating that they cannot exhibit genuinely exotic behavior beyond what arises from finite $p$-groups and their associated twists.

Methodologically, the arguments proceed by reconstructing twisted group doubles from Lagrangian subcategories of the ambient modular category. A Lagrangian subcategory encodes precisely the data needed to recover the underlying group and its cohomological twist, and its existence drives the reconstruction. This approach deliberately echoes a well-known theme in the theory of quantum groups: the characterization of doubles of quasi-Lie bialgebras through Manin pairs. In both settings, a maximal isotropic or Lagrangian structure provides the key to recovering the doubled object from its intrinsic geometry, revealing a conceptual parallel between the categorical and the Lie-theoretic contexts.

# Modular Categories of Prime Power Dimension and Group-Theoretical Structure

## Introduction

The classification of fusion categories according to their Frobenius-Perron dimension represents one of the central problems in the theory of tensor categories. This paper investigates modular categories whose Frobenius-Perron dimension is a prime power, establishing a precise structural characterization that connects these abstract categorical objects to concrete algebraic constructions arising from finite group theory.

## Main Results

The principal achievement of this work is the characterization of modular categories of prime power Frobenius-Perron dimension. We demonstrate that such categories arise precisely as the representation categories of twisted doubles of finite $p$-groups. This identification is significant because twisted doubles—also known as twisted Drinfeld doubles $D^\omega(G)$ associated to a finite group $G$ and a 3-cocycle $\omega$—provide explicit, computable examples whose properties are governed by group-theoretical data. By showing that every modular category with prime power dimension fits into this framework, we reduce the study of these categories to the more tractable domain of finite $p$-group theory and group cohomology.

Building upon this characterization, we establish a Sylow-type decomposition theorem for nilpotent braided fusion categories. In analogy with the classical structure theory for finite nilpotent groups—which decompose as direct products of their Sylow subgroups—we prove that nilpotent braided fusion categories admit a corresponding decomposition into components indexed by distinct primes. This decomposition mirrors the group-theoretical situation and reveals that the nilpotency condition in the braided categorical setting imposes rigid structural constraints closely paralleling those in finite group theory.

## Methods

The central technical tool underlying these results is a reconstruction procedure for twisted group doubles from Lagrangian subcategories of modular categories. A Lagrangian subcategory is a maximal isotropic subcategory whose Müger centralizer coincides with the subcategory itself, representing the categorical analogue of a Lagrangian subspace in symplectic geometry. When a modular category contains such a subcategory, one can recover from it a finite group together with a cohomological twist, thereby exhibiting the ambient modular category as the representation category of a twisted double. This reconstruction bridges the gap between the intrinsic categorical data and the extrinsic group-theoretical presentation.

## Consequences

A fundamental consequence of our analysis concerns modular categories with integral Frobenius-Perron dimensions. We prove that such categories are necessarily group-theoretical, meaning they can be constructed from finite groups and their cohomological data through the standard categorical operations. This property—being group-theoretical—is highly restrictive and provides substantial control over the internal structure of these categories.

The most striking application of this result lies in the theory of semisimple quasi-Hopf algebras. As a direct implication of our categorical classification, we conclude that every semisimple quasi-Hopf algebra of prime power dimension is group-theoretical. This resolves an important structural question in the theory of quasi-Hopf algebras, demonstrating that the prime power dimension hypothesis forces these algebras into the group-theoretical class. The result stands as a natural quasi-Hopf generalization of analogous theorems for ordinary Hopf algebras, and it underscores the deep interplay between the representation-theoretic properties of these algebras and the categorical framework in which they naturally reside.

# Frobenius, Perron, and Sylow: Three Pillars of Modern Mathematics

The names Frobenius, Perron, and Sylow are woven throughout the fabric of modern algebra and analysis. Though these mathematicians worked in different eras and on different problems, their contributions intersect in fascinating ways—most notably through the towering figure of Ferdinand Georg Frobenius.

## Ludwig Sylow and the Structure of Finite Groups

The Norwegian mathematician **Peter Ludwig Mejdell Sylow** (1832–1918) is remembered chiefly for the **Sylow theorems**, published in 1872. These results are among the most fundamental tools in finite group theory. Given a finite group whose order is divisible by a prime power $p^n$, the Sylow theorems guarantee:

1. **Existence** — subgroups of order $p^n$ (called Sylow $p$-subgroups) always exist.
2. **Conjugacy** — all Sylow $p$-subgroups are conjugate to one another.
3. **Counting** — the number of Sylow $p$-subgroups is congruent to $1 \pmod{p}$ and divides the order of the group.

These theorems provide a powerful lens for analyzing the internal architecture of finite groups, and they remain essential in the classification of finite simple groups.

## Frobenius as a Bridge

**Ferdinand Georg Frobenius** (1849–1917), one of Germany's most influential algebraists, deepened and extended Sylow's work. In 1887, he gave a new and elegant proof of the existence of Sylow subgroups that did not rely on group actions on cosets, and he generalized Sylow's counting results considerably. **Frobenius's theorem** on the number of solutions to $x^n = 1$ in a finite group is a direct descendant of this line of inquiry.

Frobenius also lends his name to **Frobenius groups**—transitive permutation groups in which no non-identity element fixes more than one point. Their structure, established through Frobenius's use of the emerging theory of group characters, showcases his role in founding representation theory.

## Oskar Perron and the Frobenius Connection in Linear Algebra

The link between Frobenius and **Oskar Perron** (1880–1975) lies in one of the most celebrated results in linear algebra: the **Perron–Frobenius theorem**. Perron proved the original version in 1907 for matrices with strictly positive entries, and Frobenius generalized it in 1912 to non-negative matrices.

The theorem states that a square matrix with non-negative entries possesses a real eigenvalue—the **Perron root**—that is greater than or equal to the modulus of every other eigenvalue, together with a corresponding eigenvector whose entries can be chosen to be non-negative. This result has profound applications far beyond pure mathematics:

- **Markov chains** and probability theory
- **Google's PageRank** algorithm
- **Economics** (Leontief input–output models)
- **Population dynamics** and demography

## A Legacy of Interconnection

Taken together, these three mathematicians illustrate how deep ideas cross traditional boundaries. Sylow's group-theoretic insights, sharpened by Frobenius, illuminate the algebra of symmetry; while the Perron–Frobenius theorem, born from the study of matrices, governs systems ranging from web search to ecology. Frobenius himself stands at the crossroads—collaborating in spirit with Perron and building directly upon Sylow—demonstrating the profound unity that underlies mathematics.

# Abstract

**On the Group-Theoretical Structure of Nilpotent Braided Fusion Categories**

We investigate the structure of nilpotent braided fusion categories, establishing a comprehensive framework that relates their categorical properties to the group-theoretical data underlying their construction. A braided fusion category is called nilpotent if it admits a filtration by fusion subcategories terminating in the trivial category, generalizing the classical notion of nilpotency for finite groups. Our main results demonstrate that every nilpotent braided fusion category decomposes as a Deligne tensor product of braided fusion categories whose Frobenius-Perron dimensions are prime powers, providing a categorical analogue of the decomposition of a nilpotent group into its Sylow subgroups.

We prove that nilpotent nondegenerate braided fusion categories are precisely those arising from a metric group—an abelian group equipped with a nondegenerate quadratic form—thereby yielding a complete classification in the pointed case via pre-metric group cohomology. For the general nilpotent case, we show that any such category is a group-theoretical fusion category, and we characterize when it is equivalent to a category of representations of a twisted quantum double. Furthermore, we analyze the interplay between the nilpotency class, the Müger center, and the anisotropic structure of the associated symmetric subcategories.

As applications, we obtain constraints on the possible fusion rules realizable by nilpotent braided categories, extend the notion of the upper and lower central series to the categorical setting, and derive obstructions to the existence of braidings on certain nilpotent fusion categories. Our techniques combine the theory of module categories, the de-equivariantization construction, and cohomological methods, offering new tools for the classification program of braided fusion categories. We conclude with several examples and open questions concerning the boundary between nilpotent and solvable braided fusion categories.

# Abstract

We study modular categories whose Frobenius-Perron dimension is a prime power $p^n$. Building on the classification of fusion categories of prime power dimension, we investigate the structural properties of such modular categories and their relationship to twisted doubles of finite $p$-groups. Our main results establish that every modular category of Frobenius-Perron dimension $p^n$ is nilpotent, and moreover admits a canonical decomposition reflecting its underlying $p$-group structure.

We show that a large and natural class of these categories arises as representation categories of twisted quantum doubles $D^\omega(G)$, where $G$ is a finite $p$-group and $\omega \in H^3(G, \mathbb{C}^\times)$ is a normalized $3$-cocycle. We provide necessary and sufficient conditions, formulated in terms of the abelian cocycle and the associated quadratic form on the group of invertible objects, for a pointed or nearly pointed modular category of dimension $p^n$ to be equivalent to $\mathrm{Rep}(D^\omega(G))$.

As applications, we obtain a refined classification of modular categories of dimension $p^2$ and $p^3$, exhibiting explicit families distinguished by their modular data. In particular, we compute the $S$- and $T$-matrices for twisted doubles of extraspecial and almost extraspecial $p$-groups, and we determine when non-isomorphic such groups (or inequivalent cocycles) yield equivalent modular categories. We further analyze the Witt equivalence classes and the anomaly (central charge) of these categories, relating them to the cohomology of the corresponding $p$-groups.

Our techniques combine the theory of group-theoretical and nilpotent fusion categories with cohomological computations for finite $p$-groups, and they yield new obstructions to the realization of prescribed modular data by twisted group doubles.

# Abstract

We prove that every nilpotent braided fusion category of integral Frobenius–Perron dimension is group-theoretical. Our approach exploits the structure theory of nilpotent fusion categories, which admit a canonical filtration by the adjoint subcategory and decompose, in the braided case, into a tensor product of prime components of prime-power dimension. By analyzing the symmetric centers and the associated Tannakian subcategories, we reduce the problem to understanding braided categories arising from finite groups equipped with compatible bicharacter data.

A central role is played by the correspondence between such categories and **Manin pairs**, which encode the Lagrangian data governing the braiding. We show that the integrality hypothesis forces the existence of a suitable isotropic subspace, yielding a Lagrangian subcategory whose presence is equivalent to group-theoreticity. This translates categorical nilpotency into the language of **quasi-Lie bialgebras**, where the coboundary and Jacobiator obstructions can be controlled explicitly. In particular, we interpret the associator data of a nilpotent braided fusion category as a twist deforming a classical Manin triple, and demonstrate that integrality guarantees this twist is cohomologically trivial in the relevant sense.

As consequences, we obtain that such categories are integral, that their Drinfeld centers are group-theoretical, and that any braided fusion category of odd square-free dimension is both nilpotent and group-theoretical. These results extend the classification program for fusion categories of small or structured dimension and clarify the interplay between categorical symmetry, Poisson–Lie geometry, and the deformation theory of Lie bialgebras.

# Abstract

## Characterizing Modular Categories as Representation Categories of Twisted Group Doubles

Modular tensor categories arising from the representations of twisted Drinfeld doubles $D^\omega(G)$ occupy a central position in the classification of topological orders and the construction of $(2+1)$-dimensional topological quantum field theories. In this work, we investigate necessary and sufficient conditions under which a given modular category is braided equivalent to $\mathrm{Rep}(D^\omega(G))$ for a finite group $G$ and a normalized 3-cocycle $\omega \in Z^3(G, \mathbb{C}^\times)$. We show that such categories are precisely the modular categories admitting a canonical Lagrangian algebra whose associated étale algebra structure encodes the group data, thereby recovering $G$ and the cohomology class $[\omega] \in H^3(G, \mathbb{C}^\times)$ up to isomorphism. Our approach combines the theory of module categories over pointed fusion categories with an analysis of the Frobenius-Schur indicators and the modular data $(S, T)$. We prove that a modular category is of twisted double type if and only if it contains a Tannakian (respectively, super-Tannakian) subcategory of a prescribed rank whose Müger centralizer realizes the requisite symmetry, extending earlier results on the untwisted case $\omega = 1$. As applications, we derive explicit obstructions—expressed in terms of higher Gauss sums and the Witt class of the category—that preclude certain modular categories from admitting a group-theoretical realization, and we classify all twisted doubles up to rank bounds using their fusion rules and induced Galois action. These results clarify the boundary between group-theoretical and genuinely exotic modular categories and provide computational criteria applicable to the classification program for low-rank modular data.

---

*Keywords:* modular tensor categories, twisted Drinfeld doubles, group-theoretical categories, Lagrangian algebras, 3-cocycles, topological quantum field theory
